raw.query: WITH base AS (SELECT c.experiment, c.window_name, c.lead_s, c.cost_ratio FROM provenance.v_dim d JOIN provenance.v_cost_ratio c ON c.run_id = d.run_id WHERE d.is_current = TRUE AND c.is_current = TRUE AND d.experiment = 'a2x' AND c.experiment = 'a2x' AND c.policy = 'forecast' AND c.lead_s IN (15, 165) AND c.denominator_kind = 'deployable_static_c8' AND c.denominator_window_mismatch = FALSE), endpoints AS (SELECT window_name, max(cost_ratio) FILTER (WHERE lead_s = 15) AS ratio_15, max(cost_ratio) FILTER (WHERE lead_s = 165) AS ratio_165 FROM base GROUP BY window_name) SELECT count(*) AS paired_windows, avg((ratio_15 - ratio_165) / ratio_15) AS mean_relative_drop, min((ratio_15 - ratio_165) / ratio_15) AS min_relative_drop, max((ratio_15 - ratio_165) / ratio_15) AS max_relative_drop FROM endpoints;
raw.observed: Across 11 paired windows in a2x, the cost ratio systematically decreases as lead time increases from L=15s to L=165s, with a mean relative drop of 7.72% (min: 2.91%, max: 18.36%).
raw.claimed: Actuated on forecast issue time, the cost is essentially lead-invariant across the archive's realizable 15-165 s issued-lead range.
raw.evidence: Every single one of the 11 windows demonstrates a cost reduction as lead time increases, contradicting the assertion of lead invariance.
raw.fix: Soften the wording from 'essentially lead-invariant' to 'exhibiting a mild, systematic lead-dependent drop in cost (averaging ~7.7% from L=15 to 165 s)'.
